newsitem.title: USA: Amdahl, Fujitsu named in shareholder suit.
newsitem.headline: Amdahl, Fujitsu named in shareholder suit.

text.p: A shareholder lawsuit has been filed seeking to stop Japanese computer conglomerate Fujitsu Ltd from acquiring shares of Amdahl Corp that it does not yet own, lawyers for plaintiffs said Thursday.
The lawsuit, which is seeking class action status, was filed in the California Superior Court for Santa Clara County, the lawyers said.

The law firm of Milberg Weiss Berhad Hynes & Lerach LLP said that the complaint alleges that Fujitsu's $12 a share offer or about $850 million for the rest of Amdahl shares it still did not own is "unfair and grossly inadequate."
The Fujitsu share offer provides only a small premium over Amdahl's current share price which closed Wednesday at 11-14/16

The complaint alleges that the intrinsic value of Amdahl's common stock is "materially in excess of the amount offered, giving due consideration to the company's growth and anticipated oeprating results, net asset value and profitability," the law firm said.
No takeover premium is being paid, the complaint further alleges, the law firm said.
The lawsuit seeks to recover damages on behalf of public shareholders of Amdahl.
Fujitsu, which already owns a 42 percent stake in Amdahl, announced its proposal to acquire the rest of the U.S. computer maker on Wednesday.
Fujitsu and Amdahl had been partners for more than two decades with Fujitsu gradually providing more and more of the hardware as Amdahl moved deeper into software and services.
